title: Investigate a report through its evidence and its missing test
audience: People who need to understand how strong a research claim actually is
inputs: A research brief, exact claims and citations, methods, limitations and the comparison that could change the conclusion

sources.claim: The sample discusses a hypothetical process change and shorter waits
sources.source: Authored illustrative research scenario; no actual study, result or causal finding is asserted

note: An editorial investigation, not a report read aloud. Start with a live question; separate what the source observed from what the author infers; cut to the missing comparison; narrow the conclusion; hold before the final test. The manuscript drawings are symbolic props, not facsimiles of a real publication. Replace the hypothetical waiting-time example with exact source claims and citations. Preserve methods, counterevidence and uncertainty. Use a sourced quantitative chart only when the source supplies comparable numbers; these drawings do not encode effect size. The page cuts and annotations carry the edit rather than a tour through a diagram world. Pair with the editorial treatment. See docs/source-playbooks.md.

beats.vo: A report says a new process means shorter waits. Did the process really cause the change?

props.source: Illustrative research scenario · replace with the report's exact claim

beats.vo: First separate the observation from the inference. What changed is one question. Why it changed is another.

props.source: Illustrative method · check the actual study design and evidence

beats.vo: Now find the missing comparison. What happened where the process stayed the same? What else changed at the same time?

props.source: Illustrative questions · replace with the source's actual limitations

beats.vo: Until the evidence answers that, make the claim narrower. The change followed the process. That alone does not establish its cause.

props.label: Match the claim to the evidence
props.text: A sequence is not a causal test.
props.support: State the design, the alternatives and the uncertainty.
props.source: Illustrative scenario · no actual causal finding asserted

beats.vo: End with the evidence that would change the conclusion. The most useful takeaway may be the next question to test.

props.source: Replace with the report's supported conclusion and open questions
